findings_addressed.oracle: The hex_editor package __init__.py declares __all__ = ['HexEditorPanel', 'execute_text_search', 'execute_numeric_search']. The test now asserts each of these three names is callable on the imported module, and that the deleted _ips sub-module is absent via hasattr. These are independent checks driven from the module's own declared contract.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/ui/panels/hex_editor/__init__.py, remove 'execute_text_search' from the import and __all__ list — the assertion `assert callable(getattr(mod, 'execute_text_search', None))` will fail because getattr returns None and callable(None) is False.

notes: The test previously asserted only `assert mod is not None`, which is tautological since importlib.import_module either returns the module object or raises an exception — it never returns None. The hardened version asserts three concrete callable symbols from the package's declared __all__ are present and callable, and also verifies the deleted _ips sub-module is absent from the namespace. This makes the test falsifiable: removing any export from __init__.py or re-adding an _ips binding will fail the corresponding assertion.
